reconstructed_theorem_text: Let T be a first-countable topological space, Ω a measurable space, and E a topological space equipped with a σ-algebra containing all open sets. Let μ be a probability measure on Ω and let X:T×Ω→E have a measurable slice X_t for every t∈T. Suppose for μ-almost every ω that the whole path t↦X(t,ω) is continuous on T. The map t↦(X_t)_#μ is continuous into the space of probability measures on E with the weak topology.
objects: Topological parameter space T, measurable sample space Ω, topological measurable state E, probability μ, process X and probability pushforward family.
domains: X has time slices Ω→E and sample paths T→E. Continuity of the law family is on T with values in ProbabilityMeasure E.
quantifiers: All displayed spaces, instances, μ and X are universally quantified. Slice measurability holds for every t. For μ-almost every ω, continuity holds for the whole time path.
assumptions: T is first-countable, E has measurable open sets, every slice is measurable, and the stated almost-sure path continuity holds. The statement places no compactness condition on E or joint measurability condition on X.
conclusion: The map t↦ν_t=(X_t)_#μ is weakly continuous, where ν_t(C)=μ(X_t⁻¹(C)) for measurable C⊆E.
scopes: The μ-almost-sure sample quantifier covers a full path. The compiler excerpt explicitly maps μ through X_t for each t, using the a.e. measurability witness obtained from hX t.
constant_dependencies: There is no numerical constant. The law at t uses μ and the slice X_t.
